new.s: Which metamorphic rock is formed from shale?
new.x: Shale (clay rock) changes into slate under heat and pressure; slate can further become schist.
new.angle: U0595 #6 Parent rock -> metamorphic rock (shale -> slate)

new.s: Which is the oldest rock system of India?
new.x: The Archaean system, older than 2,500 million years, is the oldest; the Tertiary is the youngest.
new.angle: U0595 #11 notes gap: oldest rock system

new.s: Which rock system of India is known for the Panna diamonds?
new.x: The Vindhyan (Purana) system of sandstone and limestone holds the Panna diamonds of Madhya Pradesh.
new.angle: U0595 #11 notes gap: Vindhyan -> Panna diamonds

new.s: In which basin of Andhra Pradesh are oil and natural gas found?

new.angle: U0595 #14 PYQ y1a603e0dbfc AP rock system -> oil

new.s: Which is the softest mineral on the Mohs scale of hardness?
new.x: The Mohs scale runs from talc (1), the softest, to diamond (10), the hardest.
new.angle: U0595 #4 notes gap: Mohs scale

new.s: Which State has the largest area of black cotton (regur) soil formed from Deccan Trap basalt?

new.s: Markapur in Andhra Pradesh is famous for which rock industry?

new.s: Mangampeta in the Cuddapah basin of Andhra Pradesh is known for which mineral?
new.x: Mangampeta holds barytes; Araku has bauxite and Ramagiri has gold.
new.angle: U0595 #14 notes gap: Mangampeta -> barytes

new.s: What are horsts also known as?
new.x: A horst is an uplifted block between faults, so it forms a block mountain; a sunken block (graben) forms a rift valley.
new.angle: U0596 #12 notes gap (APPSC 2022): horst = block mountain

new.s: Which of the following lakes is NOT a rift lake of the East African Rift?
new.x: Lake Victoria lies in a shallow basin between the rift arms, so it is not a rift lake; Lake Malawi lies at the rift's southern end.
new.angle: U0596 #12 notes gap (APPSC G1 2024): East African Rift lakes

new.s: What causes the earthquakes and volcanoes of the Andes?
o: Subduction of the Nazca Plate beneath the South American Plate
Collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates
Sliding along the San Andreas Fault
new.x: The Andes lie on a convergent boundary where the oceanic Nazca Plate sinks under the South American Plate.
new.angle: U0596 #5 PYQ y5332a37dbe2 region -> plates causing earthquakes

new.s: In which year did Alfred Wegener put forward the theory of continental drift?
new.x: Wegener gave continental drift in 1912; Holmes (1930s), Hess (1961) and plate tectonics (1967) came later.
new.angle: U0596 #1 notes gap: Wegener -> year

new.s: Which force produces a normal fault?
new.x: A normal fault forms under tension, with the hanging wall moving down; reverse and thrust faults form under compression.
new.angle: U0596 #12 notes gap: normal fault -> force

new.s: Which fossil flora is cited as an evidence of continental drift?
new.x: Glossopteris fossils occur in India and the other southern continents, showing they were once joined in Gondwanaland.
new.angle: U0596 #1 notes gap: fossil evidence (Glossopteris)

new.s: Which of the following is a volcanic mountain?

new.s: Which of the following is a young fold mountain range?

new.s: Mount Everest lies in which type of mountains?
new.x: Everest is in the Himalayas, which are young fold mountains; the world's highest peaks lie in young fold mountains.
new.angle: U0597 #4 mountain type holding the highest peaks

new.s:
Consider the following statements about earthquakes:
1. An earthquake is a geological disaster, not an atmospheric one.
2. The time, place and magnitude of an earthquake can now be predicted accurately.

new.s: In which year did the world's largest recorded earthquake, of magnitude 9.5, strike Chile?

new.s: Japan, the most earthquake-prone nation of the world, lies on which seismic belt?

new.s: Which seismic zones together cover about 56% of India's area?
